pairs.subject: read-serving-replicas
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:587 Storage::connect opens one local SQLite file in WAL mode through an 8-connection in-process pool. There is no leader, no standby and no replicated log, so the subject's precondition (a single-leader service whose standbys serve reads) does not hold; searching crates/core for replica, standby, leader and applied_index found zero hits.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:566 The only commit-driven invalidation is trigger_generation, an in-process counter bumped after commit. It is not a replica-side stream fed by a replicated log, so the technique's precondition is absent.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:587 The single read-write store has no read-only shim and no authority to forward to.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:587 Every request runs on the one writer, so there is no forward path.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:587 There are no replica caches and no accepted/applied/invalidated index to report.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:587 There are no peers to fan invalidations out to.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:587 Reads and writes hit the same local database, so read-your-writes holds trivially.
